title: BNCI 2020-001 Reach-and-Grasp Electrode Comparison EEG dataset
description: EEG recordings from healthy participants performing self-initiated natural reach-and-grasp actions (palmar and lateral grasps) with three recording systems: gel-based laboratory EEG, water-based mobile EEG, and dry-electrode mobile EEG. The movements were actually executed, not imagined. The dataset supports comparison of electrode technologies for decoding movement-related cortical activity in brain-computer interface applications. It is described in Schwarz et al. (2020, Frontiers in Neuroscience) and provided in BIDS format through the MOABB benchmark collection.
methods_description: EEG was recorded at 256 Hz from 58 EEG and 6 EOG channels using a 5% grid montage with gel-based (g.tec USBamp/g.Ladybird), water-based (EEG-Versatile) and dry-electrode (EEG-Hero) systems. Participants performed 80 self-initiated palmar and 80 lateral reach-and-grasp trials each. Offline preprocessing included 0.3-60 Hz Butterworth bandpass filtering, extended infomax ICA for gel and water systems, amplitude thresholding, and joint probability/kurtosis-based rejection.
